title: No Logical Person Would Do This
author: Kelly McGinnis
summary: Kelly McGinnis writes from her couch at midnight, asking whether leaving a twenty-year corporate career to build something of her own is worth it. She lays out what she gave up, including a paycheck, insurance and a title, and what she gained, which is complete control over what gets built and said. She acknowledges that control means the floor is hers too, and describes how she hedged by keeping consulting income while carrying several jobs at once. The deeper fear is not money but the faces of people who doubted her, the prospect of a muted launch, and the possibility that the world is simply built so the house always wins. A friend's well-meant advice to keep one foot in the old career leads her to see that a hedge becomes the outcome and that halfway guarantees failure. Delaying her launch by a few weeks shows her that her fear and her care are the same thing, and she resolves to build with fear alongside her rather than wait for it to leave.
points: Leaving a secure role trades guaranteed income and identity for full control, and that control cuts both ways because all of the risk is also yours.
She softens risk deliberately by keeping consulting income, but admits that this reduces the danger without erasing it.
The core fear is not financial: it is the satisfaction of doubters who were right about her and the possibility that the structure of the world makes the effort futile.
Advice to keep one foot in the door assumes failure ('when', not 'if') and a hedge that visibly braces for failure undermines the thing being built.
Moving the launch date shows that caution and conviction are the same impulse: you only guard something carefully if you believe it will matter.
quotes: But tonight I wanted comfort more than I wanted to be correct, and that choice is its own small headline, because for most of my life I would have taken the desk.
Control runs both directions, though. When all of it is yours, the floor is yours too.
I set it up this way on purpose, to keep us steady while I chase something that comes with no guarantees. It softens the risk. It does not erase it.
Halfway is how you guarantee the thing never works. You cannot ask people to trust something while you are visibly braced for it to fail.
The word that stayed with me was when. The failure already assumed, the soft landing already built into his sentence, the way back already drawn on the map.
The same woman lying awake certain no one will want this is the one who refused to put it out before it was right. Those look like opposites. They are the same thing from two sides.
I did not pick it up because the fear had passed. It has not, and I have stopped expecting it to. It is here on the couch tonight.
I have done safe. Twenty years of safe, and safe had its own kind of terror, the one where nothing is at risk because nothing is yours.
